claims.statement: The organization-name field accepts a chosen name. This is not a unique-name validation, completed account creation, rename permission or authorization to change repository identity.

In FPT/GHEC, GitHub Free organizations have limited private-repository features; the fragment collectively describes upgrades to Team or Enterprise Cloud for additional private/org features, with SAML and support examples. This is not proof that every named feature belongs to both plans; exact entitlement remains linked-plan review work. Product variables and more-info/trial includes resolve to the named plans and reference pointers, not a current purchase or trial receipt.

The FPT/GHEC branch states a 100,000-repository ownership limit per organization and suggests additional organizations for more repositories. This is not an estate topology mandate, permission to provision accounts, verified limit enforcement, or authority to bypass independent policies.

Organization rulesets may target all repositories, a static selected list, or dynamic naming/property filters. Deployment-context filtering is only in the virtual-registry branch, whose pinned feature applies FPT/GHEC. Linked property/ruleset guides remain separate review work.

Only organization owners edit the containing organization ruleset; repository admins or custom roles with edit-repository-rules permission can add repository rulesets. Their rules aggregate with organization rules, so new branch/tag rules cannot weaken those organization rules. This is not proof of actual activation, bypass coverage or every independent permission interaction.

Property targeting chooses Repositories matching a filter, uses a query or selection dialog, selects custom/system properties and values, and applies. The private/team/negative-language query is an example, not an executed estate target or semantic property validation.

All repositories targets the organization-wide set; Only selected repositories builds a static list by searching and selecting each repository. Neither mode proves complete real target inventory or verified enforcement.

Dynamic name targeting uses fnmatch include/exclude patterns, permits multiple criteria and may exclude a specifically named match; the cat patterns are examples. Prevent renaming of target repositories is optional. Naming matching is not RE2 validation or authority to rename/lock repositories; the linked syntax anchor remains separate context.

Deployment-context targeting requires linked-artifact records: deployable means an active storage record and deployed an active deployment record. The filter dialog accepts deployed:true or deployable:true before Apply. These metadata predicates are not running-service health, actual successful deployment, or an enforced native rollout.

Outside collaborators on private repositories consume a paid license, except the FPT free-plan branch; GHEC additionally names internal repositories. Branch-specific billing references are not actual license allocation, spending approval or rights clearance.

Outside collaborators need separate access additions to forks they should access. For GHEC private/internal forks, the collaborator must be an enterprise member or already have upstream access. Upstream access alone is not automatically all-fork access; no collaborator was added.

The incomplete prefix limits an unnamed action to organization owners or repository admins. The action and containing context are missing, so it cannot support a universal grant to either role, a defined control or actual authorized mutation.
